newsitem.title: USA: Armey to introduce auto insurance bill.
newsitem.headline: Armey to introduce auto insurance bill.

text.p: House Majority Leader Richard Armey said Tuesday he is introducing a bill to give people a choice between their state's regular auto insurance system or a new alternative "first party" system.
Under the alternative, they would have to give up the option of trying to recover non-economic damages, for pain and suffering, the Texas Republican said in a statement.
In exchange, they would get lower premiums and would also receive prompt recovery of their economic losses. The losses would be paid by the driver's own insurance company.
A similar bill has been introduced in the Senate by Mitch McConnell, a Kentucky Republican.

Armey, who plans to release details on Wednesday, said his legislation would reduce excessive litigation and fraud, and cut auto insurance costs by about a third, or $243 for an average consumer each year.
